agent: register-conventions: __cdecl signatures that really take their arguments in registers
question: checkSignatures.py cannot tell a __cdecl signature with stack parameters from a function that takes its arguments in registers - both predict a bare `ret`. Correct FindPersistentById (0x69DA00), then sweep every __cdecl entry in project.json with at least one parameter and a bare ret, and decide from the call sites whether the arguments are really pushed.

addresses.name: FindPersistentById
addresses.comment:
Looks a saved object up by its type and id - the two halves of the `id = { type = N id = N }` pair the save writes. Type 0x25 is a leader: CKillLeaderEffect::GetLeader calls it with that and the id from the event file. The name is BiceLib's.

**It takes both arguments in registers and nothing on the stack.** EAX holds the address of the key pair - two dwords, `{type, id}` - and ECX holds the hash table; the result comes back in EAX and is NULL when nothing matches. All 427 call sites set EAX with a `lea` of a stack local in the instruction immediately before the call and push nothing at all, and none of them cleans any stack afterwards.

The body: `edi = [eax]` (type), `esi = [eax+4]` (id), hashes `(type << 16) + id` by dividing it by `[ecx+4]` (the bucket count) and indexes `[ecx+8]` (the bucket array) with the remainder, then walks the chain - `[node]` is the stored pointer, `[node+4]` the next node - comparing `[stored+8]` against the type and `[stored+0xC]` against the id. So the registered object keeps its own copy of the key pair at +8/+0xC, which is where CReferenceObject's unread +0x8 and +0xC most likely go - that last step is inference, not something checked.

The table is one of two globals, `[0x1A857F4]` and `[0x1A857F0]`, and 374 of the 427 sites choose between them with `cmp <type>, 0x1268` immediately before - so the type space is split into two registries at 4712. 132 of the 427 sites follow the call with `add eax, -8` before using the result; what that adjustment reaches has not been settled here.
addresses.evidence:
Confirmed against the image, not taken from the earlier note. BODY (disasm.py rva:0x69DA00, VA 0xA9DA00, 0x55 bytes, int3 padding from 0xA9DA55): `push ebp / mov ebp, esp / and esp, -8 / push esi / mov esi, [eax+4] / push edi / mov edi, [eax]` - the first two instructions that read anything read it through EAX, before any stack slot could be touched. cfg.walk over the whole body finds NO memory operand based on ebp with a displacement of 8 or more, and none based on esp at all (checked mechanically over all 43 decoded instructions), so there is no [ebp+8] or [ebp+0xC] anywhere - the recorded `(int type, int id)` names two stack slots the function never reads. The hash is `mov eax, edi / shl eax, 0x10 / add eax, esi / xor edx, edx / div [ecx+4]`, the bucket is `mov eax, [ecx+8] / mov edx, [eax+edx*4]`, and the compare is `mov eax, [edx] / mov ecx, [eax+8] / add eax, 8 / cmp [eax+4], esi / cmp ecx, edi`. Both exits are a bare `ret` (0xA9DA4C returning 0 from `xor eax, eax`, 0xA9DA54 returning `[edx]`), which is exactly why checkSignatures.py was silent: __cdecl with two stack ints and a register convention both predict `ret 0`.

CALL SITES - the part that decides it. findRefs.py --callers 0xA9DA00 gives 427 direct calls, and all 427 were lined up against their enclosing function start (image.functionStart, decoding forward so no instruction boundary is guessed) and examined by script. In every one of the 427 the last instruction to write EAX before the call is a `lea` of a stack slot - 405 `lea eax, [esp+N]`, 20 `lea eax, [esp]`, 2 `lea eax, [ebp-N]` - so there is no site where EAX is left to chance. Not one site cleans the stack after the call: the instruction following is `test` or `cmp` 240 times, `mov` 102, `jmp` 73, `xor` 7, and never an `add esp` or a `pop` of an argument. Counting pushes in the ten instructions before each call: 375 sites have none at all, 49 have one, 3 have two or three - and all of the multi-push sites were read by hand (0x9ADC7E, 0x9F55B4, 0x9F56D8), where the pushes are `push ebx / push esi / push edi` register saves in the caller's own prologue, not arguments. Three sites read end to end: 0x54B170-0x54B1A5 loads the pair out of an object (`mov eax, [esi+0x40] / mov ecx, [esi+0x44]`) into [esp+8] and [esp+0xC], picks the table with `cmp eax, 0x1268`, then `lea eax, [esp+8] / call`; 0x9ADC66 writes the literal type (`mov dword [esp+0x10], 0x25`) and the id into the adjacent slot and passes `lea eax, [esp+0x10]`; 0x9F55A0 does the same with type 0x26. That the two dwords are written into ADJACENT slots and the address of the first is handed over is what makes them one key pair in EAX rather than two arguments pushed in the wrong order.

WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: a single call site that pushes its arguments and then does `add esp, 8`, or that reaches the call without having just lea'd a stack pair into EAX - either would mean the stack signature was right somewhere and EAX incidental. A read of [ebp+8] or [ebp+0xC] anywhere in the body would show the same, and there is none. If the pair at [eax]/[eax+4] were ever filled in the other order - id first, type second - the parameter would still be right but the field order in the comment would be backwards; the three sites read by hand all put the small literal type first, and the 0x1268 comparison at 374 sites is against that same first dword. The `@EAX` on the return would be wrong if any caller ignored EAX and read the answer elsewhere, and none does: every site tests, compares, stores or adjusts EAX immediately. `table@ECX` would be wrong if some site reached the call without writing ECX; 316 sites load it from [0x1A857F4], 11 from [0x1A857F0] and 99 from a register that holds one of those, and the one site where the write is further back than twelve instructions still does not push anything.
addresses.revises: wave 3 register-convention sweep: the recorded `void* __cdecl FindPersistentById(int type, int id)` invents two stack parameters. The function reads no stack slot at all - the key pair's address arrives in EAX and the hash table in ECX - and all 427 call sites push nothing and clean nothing. Both readings end in a bare `ret`, so checkSignatures.py could not see it; only the call sites can. Left as recorded, Ghidra types [ebp+8] and [ebp+0xC] as the type and the id in 427 callers that never wrote them, and the two registers the call really uses decompile as uninitialised.

slots_noted: 0xA9DA00 is in no class's virtual table - mergeFindings.inTables() returns nothing for it, and it is a free function reached only by direct call, 427 of them. It is the only function this file names, so no slot anywhere is affected.
swept: The sweep behind the one correction, so it is a measured result rather than a list of hits. project.json holds 46 function entries whose signature says __cdecl; 8 take no parameters and are not candidates, leaving 38 with at least one. All 38 end in a bare `ret` (checkSignatures' own cfg.walk over each; `atoi` at 0x7969F1 and `free` at 0x795F9B reach theirs through a hotpatch thunk `mov edi,edi / push ebp / mov ebp,esp / pop ebp / jmp`, and `operator_new` at 0x79602F also reports a `ret 16` that belongs to code past its own `ret` at 0xB96054). Each was examined mechanically for reads of an incoming argument slot - a memory operand at [ebp+8] or above, or at [esp+N] in a function with no ebp frame. 24 of the 38 declare at least one stack parameter, and 23 of those read exactly the argument slots they declare: LogRecord::Make 0x2410 reads +8/+0xC/+0x10 for its three, GetTotalBuildCost 0x63D40 +8/+0xC/+0x10/+0x14 for its four, GetManpowerDetailsText 0x2D0540 +8/+0xC, std::string::concat 0x65CC70 +8/+0xC/+0x10, std::operator<<Chars 0x21D30 +8/+0xC, _input_l 0x7A1379 +8/+0xC/+0x10/+0x14, sscanf 0x7964D4 and strtol 0x7A2D44 +8/+0xC/+0x10, and RegisterDynamicToken 0x669CA0, std::string::operatorPlusChars 0x65B150, std::endl 0x2240, GetSubUnit 0x4E9E40, GetSubUnitByIndex 0x4E9F00, std::ios_base::_Ios_base_dtor 0x794BAE, std::ios_base::_Addstd 0x794B59, free, malloc, operator_new, _callnewh, set_purecall_handler_encoded and atol each read +8 for their one, with strlen 0x79C9F0 reading [esp+4] in a function that keeps no frame. FindPersistentById was the only one of the 24 that reads no argument slot whatever. Call sites were then surveyed where it mattered: LogRecord::Make 835 sites, 692 of them exactly three pushes followed by `add esp, 0xC`; GetTotalBuildCost 3 sites, every one placing four dwords and doing `add esp, 0x10`; GetManpowerDetailsText 2 sites, both `add esp, 8`; std::string::concat 1 site, `add esp, 0xC`; std::string::operatorPlusChars 477 sites and std::endl 845 sites, with cleanup dominated by the 4 bytes their single stack parameter costs. Two could not be settled from call sites: GetSubUnit and GetSubUnitByIndex have no direct callers at all, so only their bodies speak for them - both read [ebp+8], which rules out the register error, but nothing confirms who cleans up. The remaining 14 of the 38 already spell their arguments as registers (LogRecord::Flush, CHistoricalModelSet::PickCurrentModel, CKillLeaderEffect::GetLeader, FileExists, ReportUnknownKey, ReportParseError, ParseInt, ReleaseTextReplacements, DestroyStringsInRange, ParseObjectReference, std::string::fromCString, std::ostream::writeCString, std::ostringstream::str, std::ios_base::_Init); the inverse error - a register annotation on an argument that is really pushed - is equally invisible to the ret check, so they went through the same scan, and not one of them reads an incoming argument slot either. 38 examined, 37 stand, 1 corrected.
